newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.84/85 a dlr in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.84/85 a dlr in quiet trade.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.84/85 against the dollar on a quiet Wednesday, dealers said.
The rupee had opened the day at 35.85/86 a dollar.
Poor dollar demand and normal supply, a trend seen over the last week, continued to colour the market, dealers said.
The first tranche of redemption of India Development Bonds, around $700 million, was due on Wednesday.
Newspapers had reported that a big chunk of the bonds were being converted into rupees.
The only highlight of Wednesday's trading was dollar puchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) at 35.85 level.
A poll of top company treasurers conducted by Standard Chartered Bank released on Wednesday said the rupee was expected to touch a mean of 36.03 against the dollar within one month.
The rupee was seen touching 36.35 in three months and 36.73 in six months, the poll found.

In a commentary on the poll, Standard Chartered Bank said large dollar outflows during 1997 on account of bond redemption and IMF loan repayment were known with certainty, but there was uncertainty on the dollar inflows front.
"The expected increase in the oil import bill, unlikely portfolio investments and sluggish exports should weaken the rupee, notwithstanding a buildup of reserves by the RBI."
"Exporters should still take advantage of the premium and receive forward (premia)," it said.
The forward dollar premia continued its fall on Wednesday. The six-month annualised premium closed at 7.36 percent, down from the previous close of 7.54 percent, dealers said.
